description:
CONTEXT — PREREQUISITE: flm-40e.2 (Item 1a) must be complete. WHAT PROBLEM THIS SOLVES Without memoization, every render of a component re-evaluates every sub-expression in the template, even if the inputs have not changed. React Compiler (React Forget) solves this by: 1. Grouping template sub-expressions into "reactive scopes" by shared dependencies 2. Each scope gets its own cache slot (use_memo with specific deps) 3. Object.is comparison — if deps unchanged, return cached value Filament does the same at compile time in VNodeCompiler. The ~F macro should emit use_memo calls wrapping sub-expressions instead of plain expressions. TERMINOLOGY - "reactive variable": any @foo reference in the template (after Item 1a, these are bare variables) - "reactive scope": a sub-expression whose deps are a specific subset of reactive variables - "stable value": a value that does not change across renders — setter functions (from use_state), atoms, integers, string literals KEY INSIGHT: use_state setters are stable (guaranteed by Item 0). This means closures that capture only setters are also stable and can be their own memoized scope with [] deps (empty deps = computed once, never recomputed). DEPENDENCY TRACKING ALGORITHM At compile time, for each sub-expression in the VNode tree: 1. Walk the AST to find all variable references 2. Identify which are reactive (@foo → foo after Item 1a transformation) 3. Closures: their deps are the reactive variables they capture (exclude stable setter vars) 4. Group adjacent sub-expressions with identical dep sets into one scope 5. Each scope becomes: use_memo(deps, fn -> end) EXAMPLE Given a component with: count = use_state(0) → {count, set_count} = use_state(0) # set_count is stable filter = use_state(:all) → {filter, set_filter} = use_state(:all) # set_filter is stable Template: ~F"""
{@count}
""" Compiled output (schematic): use_memo([count], fn -> {:element, :span, [], [{:text, count}]} end) |> then(fn span -> use_memo([count], fn -> # closure deps: count (set_count is stable → not a dep) {:element, :button, [on_click: fn -> set_count.(count + 1) end], [{:text, "+"}]} end) end) |> then(fn plus_btn -> use_memo([], fn -> # closure deps: none (set_filter is stable) {:element, :button, [on_click: fn -> set_filter.(:all) end], [{:text, "All"}]} end) end) |> then(fn all_btn -> {:element, :div, [], [span, plus_btn, all_btn]} end) STABLE SETTER DETECTION The compiler needs to know which variables are stable setters. Strategy: - At compile time, pattern-match on the binding site: {count, set_count} = use_state(_) - The second element of a use_state destructure is always stable - Similarly for use_observable: {value, _server} = use_observable(_) — value is reactive, _server stable (not typically used in templates) - Track these in a "stable_vars" set and exclude them from dep computation HOW TO IMPLEMENT IN VNodeCompiler Extend lib/filament/vnode_compiler.ex (built in Item 1a) with a second pass: defp infer_scopes(vnode_ast, stable_vars) do # Walk vnode_ast # For each sub-expression, compute deps = free_vars(expr) -- stable_vars # Wrap in use_memo(deps, fn -> expr end) end defp free_vars(ast) do # Collect all variable references in the AST # Exclude: module names, function names, literals end The compile/2 function first builds the raw VNode AST (Item 1a), then runs infer_scopes/2. use_memo IS ALREADY DEFINED in lib/filament/hooks.ex. Read that file for the current signature. It takes (deps, fun) and returns the cached value if deps unchanged. TESTING Run: mix test All existing tests must pass. Write tests in test/filament/vnode_compiler_test.exs: 1. A template with @count emits use_memo([count], fn -> ... end) — verify by asserting that re-rendering the component with the same count value does NOT re-evaluate the inner expression (use a counter or side-effect accumulator to detect evaluations) 2. A closure capturing only a stable setter emits use_memo([], fn -> ... end) — verify that the closure is the same function object across renders (==/2 on fn reference after two render calls) 3. A template with both @count and @filter in separate sub-expressions produces two separate scopes with their own deps Integration test: the todo example (examples/todo/) exercises all of this — after TodoList rewrite (Item 4), toggling one todo should NOT re-evaluate the VNode subtree for other todos.
title: Item 1b: VNodeCompiler — reactive scope inference (auto-memoization)
